description: Organizations designated, contracted, licensed or certified by the State of Minnesota for disability and aging services, with the counties each serves. Organizational contacts only.

categories.title: Centers for Independent Living
categories.intro: Minnesota has eight Centers for Independent Living. They are funded and overseen through Vocational Rehabilitation Services at the Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development. Each serves a set of counties. The national directory of centers lists no Minnesota center serving these counties: Big Stone, Chippewa, Lac qui Parle, McLeod, Renville, Swift. People there can call Disability Hub MN or the nearest center.
categories.designatedBy: Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development, Vocational Rehabilitation Services

entries.name: Access North Center for Independent Living of Northeastern Minnesota

categories.title: Area Agencies on Aging and Minnesota Aging Pathways
categories.intro: The Minnesota Board on Aging designates seven area agencies on aging. Six serve regions of the state and one serves American Indian elders. Minnesota Aging Pathways, formerly the Senior LinkAge Line, is the statewide line they run together.

entries.name: Arrowhead Area Agency on Aging
entries.what: Plans and funds services for older adults and family caregivers in its area, such as meals, rides, caregiver support and help at home, using federal Older Americans Act funds. Works with the Minnesota Board on Aging on Minnesota Aging Pathways. Part of the Arrowhead Regional Development Commission. Office in Duluth.

categories.title: Health plans for Special Needs BasicCare and Minnesota Senior Health Options
categories.intro: Special Needs BasicCare is for people with disabilities ages 18 to 64 who get Medical Assistance. Minnesota Senior Health Options and Minnesota Senior Care Plus are for people 65 and older. The Department of Human Services contracts with these health plans, and the choices differ by county. Counties here come from the department's maps for October 1 to December 31, 2026. The department has also published maps for 2027 with some changes. UCare offered these programs through September 30, 2026.

entries.name: Blue Plus
entries.what: Health plan under contract with the Department of Human Services. Offers Minnesota Senior Health Options or Minnesota Senior Care Plus in 87 counties, based on the department's maps for October 1 to December 31, 2026. Part of Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota.

categories.title: Disability Hub MN
categories.intro: The statewide information and help line for people with disabilities, run for the Department of Human Services Disability Services Division.
categories.designatedBy: Minnesota Department of Human Services, Disability Services Division (contract)

entries.name: Disability Hub MN
entries.what: Free statewide resource network that helps people with disabilities solve problems, find their way through services and plan for the future. Managed by the Department of Human Services Disability Services Division and delivered under contract by the Metropolitan Center for Independent Living and the Southeastern Minnesota Center for Independent Living. It replaced the Disability Linkage Line in 2017 and kept the same phone number. Phone and chat Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

source.title: Introducing Disability Hub MN (Minnesota Council on Disability)

categories.title: Licensed home and community-based services providers
categories.intro: Providers of home and community-based services for people with disabilities must hold a license under Minnesota Statutes, chapter 245D, issued by the Department of Human Services. There are thousands of license holders, so they are not listed here. Use the lookups below to find or check a provider.
categories.designatedBy: Minnesota Department of Human Services, Office of Inspector General, Licensing Division

entries.name: Department of Human Services Licensing Division (home and community-based services, chapter 245D)
alsoKnownAs: Office of Inspector General Licensing Division
entries.what: Licenses providers of home and community-based services under Minnesota Statutes, chapter 245D, such as residential supports, day services, employment services, and in-home and personal supports for people on disability waivers. A temporary pause on new 245D licenses and on adding services to existing licenses began January 1, 2026 and is expected to last until December 31, 2027, with limited exceptions requested by counties, Tribal Nations and health plans. Use the Licensing Information Lookup to check a provider's license, services and any licensing actions. Licensing help desk: 651-431-6624.

source.title: Licensing for Home and Community-Based Services: 245D providers (Department of Human Services)

categories.title: Other state-designated offices and councils
categories.intro: State offices, councils and the protection and advocacy agency that work on disability and aging rights, complaints and policy statewide.
categories.designatedBy: State law and federal designation (see each entry)

entries.name: Minnesota Board on Aging
entries.what: State board that oversees aging services under the federal Older Americans Act, designates the area agencies on aging, and runs Minnesota Aging Pathways and the Office of Ombudsman for Long-Term Care.

source.title: Department of Human Services contact numbers (Minnesota Board on Aging)

entries.name: Office of Ombudsman for Long-Term Care
entries.what: Free service of the Minnesota Board on Aging for people receiving licensed long-term care, including nursing homes, assisted living, foster care and home care. Helps residents and families resolve complaints. It does not regulate providers.

source.title: Department of Human Services contact numbers (Office of Ombudsman for Long-Term Care)

entries.name: Office of Ombudsman for Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities
entries.what: Independent state agency that takes complaints about the care and treatment people receive for mental illness, developmental disabilities, substance use disorder and emotional disturbance in children.

source.title: Contact the Office of Ombudsman for Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities

entries.name: Minnesota Disability Law Center
entries.what: The federally designated protection and advocacy agency for people with disabilities in Minnesota. Gives free civil legal help on disability-related legal problems statewide, regardless of age or income. Part of Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid.

source.title: Minnesota Disability Law Center (Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid)

entries.organizationsName: Minnesota Disability Law Center (part of Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid)

entries.name: Minnesota Governor's Council on Developmental Disabilities
entries.what: State council funded under the federal Developmental Disabilities Act. Works on policy, training and projects that increase independence, productivity and community inclusion for people with developmental disabilities and their families.

source.title: Minnesota Governor's Council on Developmental Disabilities

entries.name: Minnesota Council on Disability
entries.what: State agency that advises the Governor, the Legislature and the public on disability policy and gives technical help on accessibility and disability rights.

source.title: Contact the Minnesota Council on Disability

entries.name: MnCHOICES assessment lead agencies
entries.what: MnCHOICES assessments for long-term services and supports are done by certified assessors at lead agencies: counties, Tribal Nations and health plans. No separate public list of certified assessor agencies outside these lead agencies was found. Contact the county agency, Tribal Nation or health plan.

source.title: MnCHOICES (Department of Human Services)

lookups.name: Licensing Information Lookup
lookups.what: The Department of Human Services search of licensed programs, including 245D home and community-based services licenses. Search by name, license type, city or county to see license status, services and licensing actions. Search results can be exported to a spreadsheet file. The site may ask you to complete a security check first.

lookups.name: Minnesota Health Care Programs provider directory
lookups.what: Search for providers enrolled with Minnesota Health Care Programs for fee-for-service care. It may not list every home and community-based services provider. People in a health plan should use their plan's directory.

lookups.name: Minnesota Aging and Disability Resources
lookups.what: The state's searchable directory of services for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers. Older materials call this directory MinnesotaHelp.info.
